name: view_api_instance_policies
title: View API Instance Policies
description: Show the applied policies for one API instance, MuleSoft-hosted or external. A MuleSoft (Flex Gateway) instance is read from Anypoint API Manager with the same grouping UI as the web app; an EXTERNAL gateway instance (Kong / Apigee / Azure / AWS) has its native applied policies read through the Anypoint API Manager Universal API (gated per organization). Provider is deduced from the instance; pass provider only to force it. External policies expose scope and rules as reported by the Universal API; applicationTargets exposes resolved AWS HTTP methods and paths, including CORS paths derived from provenance when rules is empty. rules retains the upstream target representation. Do not infer INSTANCE scope from missing rules. To apply an external policy, choose a scope from the selected template's supportedScopes and pass target.scope and target.rules to apply_policy_to_instance. PATH requires a path, METHOD a method, OPERATION both, and INSTANCE no rules. pointcut_data is an apply argument for MuleSoft policies only. To edit an external policy's configuration, use edit_applied_policy with the policyId listed here.

provider.description: Optional gateway provider of the instance: 'kong', 'apigee', 'azure', or 'aws' for an external gateway, or 'mulesoft' (default). Leave empty to deduce it from the instance. For an external provider the native applied policies (with each policy's policyId, current configurationData, readOnly flag, and Exchange coordinates for edit_applied_policy) are read through the Anypoint API Manager Universal API; this routing is gated per organization.
provider.title: Provider

name: apply_policy_to_instance
title: Apply Policy To Asset Instance
description: Apply the selected policy to a SINGLE target asset instance using the provided configuration data. This is the tool for a provider-NATIVE policy (a Kong plugin name or an Apigee template ID, as selected via prepare_policy_creation) — those are NOT canonical templates and can only be applied one instance at a time, so loop this tool per instance if a native policy targets several. It is also the right choice for a single MuleSoft/Anypoint instance when you need fine per-instance control (order, pointcut, disabled). ONLY for a CANONICAL (Universal) policy — one returned by 'list_universal_policies' — that must be applied to MORE THAN ONE API instance at once, or across instances spanning different providers (mulesoft/anypoint, kong, apigee, azure, aws), prefer 'apply_universal_policy' instead: it fans the canonical template out across every instance in one call and creates the native policy on each provider's control plane. Do NOT route a native plugin/template id to 'apply_universal_policy' — it only accepts canonical template names. For a non-MuleSoft external gateway (provider='kong'/'apigee'/'azure'/'aws'), set provider and pass the numeric api_instance_id plus the template's Exchange coordinates via asset (group_id + asset_id + asset_version, from get_policy_template_form) — the policy is applied through the Anypoint API Manager Universal API (gateway_id is not used on this path). injection_point is optional; omit it to let APIM default it from the template. This routing is gated per organization; a closed gate returns a structured error. Follow this order: select the native policy using prepare_policy_creation, load its detail using get_policy_template_form, then offer only the scopes returned in template.supportedScopes. Do not ask for scope before the selected template is loaded. After the user chooses a scope, collect its required path/method and the configuration fields from the template schema. Pass target={scope: 'INSTANCE'} for the whole instance, target={scope: 'PATH', rules: [{path: '/orders'}]} for a path, target={scope: 'METHOD', rules: [{method: 'GET'}]} for a method, or target={scope: 'OPERATION', rules: [{method: 'GET', path: '/orders'}]} for an operation. For external native policies, omit pointcut_data entirely: that argument is MuleSoft-only. Use target.scope and target.rules; do not reuse methodRegex/uriTemplateRegex from view_api_instance_policies as apply arguments. The tool sends scope and rules to the Universal API. When choosing a scope, pass it explicitly in target.scope. INSTANCE needs no targets. Omitted target preserves APIM defaults for templates that only support INSTANCE or declare no supportedScopes; templates supporting other scopes require target. For a non-INSTANCE scope, do not call apply until the user has supplied its required targets, even when it is the template's only scope. CORS allowMethods config does not select the application path or method. Use the targets selected by the user; never silently choose a scope or endpoint.

PolicyApplicationTarget.description: User-selected scope and targets, separate from policy configuration.
PolicyApplicationTarget.title: PolicyApplicationTarget

Optional Exchange asset coordinates for a policy template.

``group_id`` / ``asset_id`` / ``asset_version`` triple that callers
must keep in sync.
PolicyApplyAssetRef.title: PolicyApplyAssetRef

PolicyConfigurationData.description:
Open-shape configuration object passed to API Manager when applying a policy.

The exact key set is policy-template-specific (e.g. rate-limiting uses
``rateLimits``; OAuth2 uses ``tokenUrl``). ``extra='allow'`` preserves
template-defined keys; clients can still receive a structured JSON schema
in the tool spec instead of an unconstrained ``dict``.
PolicyConfigurationData.title: PolicyConfigurationData

PolicyPointcutData.description:
Open-shape pointcut filter that scopes a policy to subset of requests.

Shape is defined by the resource-level policy template. ``extra='allow'``
keeps the envelope typed without pinning template-specific keys.
PolicyPointcutData.title: PolicyPointcutData

target.description: External gateway apply scope chosen by the user from template.supportedScopes. INSTANCE has no rules; PATH rules contain path; METHOD rules contain method; OPERATION rules contain both method and path. First select the native policy and load get_policy_template_form; only then offer the scopes returned in template.supportedScopes. After the scope is chosen, collect its concrete targets before applying. Never ask for scope before loading the selected template. Required when an external template does not support INSTANCE. Omission preserves APIM instance defaults when INSTANCE is supported or supportedScopes is not declared. If INSTANCE is the only supported scope, pass target={scope: INSTANCE} without asking for a path or method. For any non-INSTANCE scope, collect its required destinations even if it is the only supported scope.

name: list_environments
title: List Environments
description: Use this tool to list the Anypoint environments in a business group, with each environment's type reliably resolved to sandbox / production / unknown (field `environmentType`). Read-only: it does NOT change the active-environment context (that is `select_active_environment`). Resolves the org from the session when `organization_id` is omitted. Use for prompts like 'list the environments in my sandbox business group', 'which environments does org X have?', 'do I have a production environment?'. Example: list_environments(organization_id=<organization_id>).

Resolves the org from the session when `organization_id` is omitted. Use for prompts like 'create a sandbox environment called QA', 'add a production environment to org X'. name: get_my_profile
title: Get My Profile
description: Use this tool to view the current user's own profile / personal settings. Read-only. Returns the caller's identity (username, email, name) and the business groups they belong to. Sensitive fields (phone, last-login, IdP linkage) and permission grants are deliberately omitted — this does NOT report roles or permissions. Use for prompts like 'show my profile', 'what's my email on file?', 'which business groups am I in?'. Example: get_my_profile().

name: list_apis
title: List APIs
description: List APIs from the MuleSoft Platform catalog for a given organization. Presents an interactive UI for browsing, filtering, and selecting APIs. Paginated: pass offset/limit; if the response has has_more=true, request the next page with the returned next_offset. To find a specific API by name or topic, prefer find_assets over paging through the whole list. If the user has not said whether public catalog assets should be included, ask them to clarify before searching, then pass include_public explicitly.

include_public.description: Whether to include MuleSoft public-catalog APIs alongside private organization assets. Ask the user to clarify this scope when their request does not specify it, then pass the choice explicitly.
include_public.title: Include Public

name: list_business_groups
title: List Business Groups
description: List available business groups, optionally filtering by name. Paginated: pass offset/limit; if the response has has_more=true, request the next page with the returned next_offset.

name: find_assets
title: Find Assets
description:
🔍 Discover assets in your portfolio + the public catalog.

Use this tool for any of:
  ✓ 'find [thing]' / 'search for [thing]' / 'discover [thing]'
  ✓ 'do you have [thing]?' / 'is there a [thing]?'
  ✓ 'show me [thing]' / 'list [thing]' / 'what [things] exist?'
  ✓ Data catalog discovery ('show my data assets', 'find Informatica sources')
  ✓ '[type] for [capability]' (e.g. 'APIs for payments', 'agents for invoices')
  ✓ 'similar to [thing]' / 'alternatives to [thing]'
  ✓ Resolving a user-supplied display name or slug to an asset id
    before navigating or fetching detail.

Internally runs the same lexical (literal slug / short query / id-token /
prefix) discovery the catalog UI and cmd-k use, so results match what a
user sees on screen for the same words. One call covers literal pastes
('pet-store-api'), partial names ('Pet Store'), and single tokens
('store'). It does NOT do concept/synonym matching — a paraphrase that
shares no words with the asset's name/description/tags may not match.

SEARCH DISCIPLINE (prefer one natural-language call):
  Lexical search already handles slug / hyphen / spacing variants, so a
  phrase like 'batch processing agent' already matches — slugging
  the same intent into 'batch-processing' or 'batch processing' and re-calling
  rarely surfaces anything new. Aim for ~3 calls at most, with at least one
  using ASSET_TYPE="" (no filter). Empty results usually mean nothing matched;
  slug/spacing rewrites of the same intent seldom help — though rephrasing for
  a genuinely different angle (e.g. a broader or analytical query) is fine.

Returns userOrgAssets (your portfolio) + publicOrgAssets (MuleSoft public
catalog), each ranked by relevance.

USER_QUERY parameter (always pass it):
  The user's verbatim, untrimmed message. Used only to tell a single named
  lookup ('the NTO Recommendations API' → collapse the card to that asset)
  from a set/category ('all finance APIs', 'APIs similar to Stripe' → keep
  the whole set). Never sent to the search backend; pass even when you also
  trim QUERY down to the key search terms.

ASSET_TYPE parameter (optional):
  Leave empty ("") to search ALL types (recommended for discovery).
  Pass when the user clearly names ONE kind:
    'api' / 'apis' → expands to 'rest-api', 'http-api', 'graphql', 'soap-api', 'grpc-api', 'evented-api' (EXCLUDES 'mcp', 'agent', 'llm', 'model', 'vector-database', 'gateway')
    'mcp', 'agent', 'llm' for those kinds
    'data' for Informatica/CDGC data assets and catalog sources

APPLIED POLICIES (INCLUDE_APPLIED_POLICIES + POLICY_NAME_FILTER):
  Set INCLUDE_APPLIED_POLICIES=true to answer 'which of my APIs have / are
  missing policy X?' in ONE call. Each of your portfolio results then also
  carries the policies currently APPLIED to its managed instances (MuleSoft
  and external Kong/Apigee/Azure). Pass POLICY_NAME_FILTER='rate-limiting'
  (name or substring) to report the found/missing split directly — do NOT
  loop view_api_instance_policies over every hit. For the apply flow key on
  policyCoverage ('all'/'partial'/'none'/'unknown') + instancesMissingPolicy
  (the instances still lacking it), NOT hasPolicy alone: hasPolicy is
  any-instance, so a partially-protected API reads True and would be skipped.
  Off by default; the fan-out is bounded (top matched APIs, production-first
  instances) and the meta block says what was capped.

DO NOT USE FOR:
  ✗ Performance metrics (use fetch_monitoring_*)
  ✗ Cost analysis (use fetch_cost_*)
  ✗ Governance findings / conformance reports (use fetch_governance_*) — but
    for APPLIED policies across a set of APIs, use INCLUDE_APPLIED_POLICIES
    above rather than calling view_api_instance_policies per asset.
  ✗ Applied policies for ONE already-known instance (use view_api_instance_policies)
  ✗ Already-selected asset details (use asset-specific tools)
  ✗ Typed catalog listings (use fetch_services)
  ✗ Catalog facets / aggregates (use fetch_service_facets)
